candidates.title: PriorityFEC: Deadline-Aware Streaming FEC for KV-Cache Handoff in Edge Multi-Agent Systems
candidates.abstract: Collaborative edge large language model (LLM) systems often require repeated prefill computation when task contexts are transferred between agents. Reusing previously computed key--value (KV) caches can eliminate this overhead, but requires KV-cache delivery before the receiving agent begins decoding. Under strict deadlines and unreliable edge links, complete KV cache transfer may be infeasible, making the timely delivery of useful KV information critical. This paper proposes PriorityFEC, a utility-aware KV-cache handoff scheme that combines prioritized source transmission with adaptive loss recovery. PriorityFEC first organizes KV blocks into a utility-aware source queue to prioritize important information. It then employs ACK-sliding Streaming FEC and a lightweight Double Deep Q-Network (Double-DQN) scheduler to dynamically balance source delivery and repair transmission under deadline constraints. We implement PriorityFEC in a distributed edge LLM-serving prototype and evaluate it using Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct across multiple workloads. Experimental results demonstrate that PriorityFEC preserves more useful KV information and achieves substantially higher task accuracy than competing transport schemes, particularly when the deadline is insufficient to deliver the complete KV cache.
candidates.reason: Edgeのmulti-agent LLMで前段agentのKVを次のagentへ渡す際、無線リンクの損失とTTFT締切のため全KV転送が間に合わない問題を扱う。重要度の高いKV blockを先に送るutility-aware streamと、受信feedbackに基づき期限までにrepair packetを配置するStreaming FECを統合するPriorityFECを提案。Qwen2.5-7BとLlama-3.1-8Bの分散edge serving試作で、厳しい期限下ほど既存転送方式よりタスク品質が良いと報告。KV再利用とネットワーク転送の直接最適化なのでaccept。

candidates.title: PACE: Pareto-Adaptive Compression for Efficient Native MLLMs
candidates.abstract: Native multimodal large language models (native MLLMs) jointly encode visual and linguistic sequences within a unified autoregressive Transformer, emerging as a promising paradigm for multimodal understanding. Unlike conventional ViT-based MLLMs relying on external vision encoders, ViT-free native MLLMs tokenize pixel patches directly, potentially suffering severe visual token redundancy. A pilot study confirms this: unlike ViT-based models that degrade under compression, ViT-free MLLMs tolerate aggressive compression with near-lossless or even improved performance. Yet existing compression methods target ViT-based settings, leaving native MLLMs, which stand to gain the most, unexplored. To close this gap, we introduce an analysis pipeline centered on token discriminability and cross-dimensional heterogeneous redundancy, revealing that (i) redundancy is distributed independently and heterogeneously along height and width axes, and (ii) early-layer visual tokens are indiscriminable and uniformly redundant. Guided by these findings, we propose PACE (Pareto-Adaptive Compression for Efficient Native MLLMs), the first visual token compression framework tailored for native MLLMs with Multimodal-RoPE. Leveraging dimensional decoupling of positional encoding, PACE decomposes attention into two orthogonal spatial saliency estimates along height and width, gated by a positional attention signal, yielding direction-aware importance with negligible overhead. It further casts token budget allocation as Pareto optimization over performance preservation, inference efficiency, and spatial coverage, jointly identifying optimal compression depths and retention ratios. Experiments show PACE maintains near-lossless performance at only 25%-50% visual token retention, even improving several benchmarks, while delivering over 2x FLOPs reduction.
candidates.reason: ViTを持たず画像patchを直接token化するnative MLLM向けに、空間の縦横軸ごとにattention重要度を推定し、Multimodal-RoPEと整合する視覚token削減を行うPACEを提案。保持性能・推論効率・空間網羅性のPareto最適化で層とtoken保持率を選ぶ。NeurIPS 2026採択版の一次要旨では視覚tokenを25〜50%保持して性能を概ね維持し、FLOPsを2倍超削減と報告。推論token数と計算量の直接改善なのでaccept。
